To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a deadline-differentiated forward contract for deferrable electric load can achieve efficient resource allocation and incentive compatibility, when combined with EDF scheduling.
a deadline-differentiated price scheme, in combination EDF scheduling, induces truthful revelation of deadlines and yields efficient outcomes.

(1) a non-discriminating deadline-differentiated electricity pricing scheme can be used to elicit the true deadline of each consumer and induce an optimal EDF scheduling policy for the system; (2) a deadline-differentiated forward contract can be used to induce the desired response from consumers; and (3) the proposed scheme is incentive compatible, in that each consumer would prefer to report her true deadline to maximize her expected utility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of forward electricity markets that provide a flexible and efficient mechanism for integrating large quantities of deferrable electric demand.
the design of forward markets for deadline-differentiation of electricity demand.

the design of an efficient, incentive compatible, forward market that enables the supplier to efficiently absorb the variability in renewable generation and the consumer to realize her preferred trade-off between price and delivery deadline for her load.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel market mechanism for deadline differentiated electric power service, and we prove that this market mechanism is incentive compatible, non-discriminative and efficient.

the proposed forward contract, in combination with the EDF scheduling policy and the efficient pricing scheme, provides a complete mechanism for the design of a deadline-differentiated market for deferrable electric loads.
deadline differentiated pricing of deferrable electric loads is a viable and efficient mechanism to absorb variability in renewable generation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a deadline-differentiated, forward electricity market with EDF scheduling is incentive compatible and yields a competitive equilibrium.
we propose a forward market for deadline differentiated power service, and show that the market is incentive compatible and yields an efficient outcome.
a non-discriminating, deadline-differentiating pricing scheme is incentive-compatible and efficient in the presence of EDF scheduling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed forward contract, in combination with deadline-differentiated energy pricing and EDF scheduling, provides a mechanism that can induce consumers to reveal their true deadlines to the supplier, thereby allowing the supplier to efficiently allocate the available supply to the consumers with the most stringent deadlines.

a simple deadline-differentiated forward contract can induce the desired response of deferrable loads in a decentralized, non-discriminative manner, and that the EDF scheduling policy is optimal to achieve the desired response.

a forward market for deadline differentiated energy services, in combination with a simple EDF scheduling policy, can be used to induce consumers to reveal their true deadlines, and thereby to achieve efficient allocation of energy resources.
